subject: Neurology
vignette: A 34-year-old woman develops a severe headache and vomiting over several days. Imaging reveals a mass effect raising intracranial pressure. Funduscopy shows elevated optic discs with blurred margins bilaterally.
question: Which of the following best explains the mechanism of these funduscopic findings?

options.text: Increased intracranial pressure impairing axoplasmic flow in the optic nerves
Increased intraocular pressure causing optic disc cupping

explanation_correct: Papilledema is bilateral optic disc swelling due to increased intracranial pressure, for example from mass effect. The elevated pressure impairs axoplasmic flow within the optic nerve, leading to disc elevation and blurred margins. It must be distinguished from glaucoma-related cupping due to high intraocular pressure and from optic neuritis.

explanation_incorrect.B: Elevated intraocular pressure causes glaucomatous cupping, not the bilateral disc swelling seen with impaired axoplasmic flow.
explanation_incorrect.C: Retinal arterial occlusion produces a cherry-red spot and pale retina, not disc swelling from raised intracranial pressure.
explanation_incorrect.D: Demyelination (optic neuritis) causes painful monocular vision loss, not bilateral pressure-related disc swelling.
explanation_incorrect.E: Choroidal neovascularization is a feature of wet AMD with bleeding, not papilledema.

educationalObjective: Papilledema is bilateral optic disc swelling from increased ICP impairing axoplasmic flow, distinct from glaucomatous cupping.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 2-year-old is brought in because a flash photograph shows a white reflection in the child's left pupil instead of the normal red reflex. The parents report occasional eye misalignment.
question: Which of the following is the most important cause that must be ruled out in this child?
explanation_correct: Leukocoria is loss or whitening of the red reflex and in children importantly suggests retinoblastoma or congenital cataract. Retinoblastoma is the most common intraocular malignancy in children, arises from immature retinal cells with mutations in both RB1 tumor suppressor genes on chromosome 13, and presents with leukocoria, strabismus, nystagmus, or eye redness.

explanation_incorrect.A: Allergic conjunctivitis causes itchy red eyes with discharge, not a white pupillary reflex.
explanation_incorrect.C: Viral conjunctivitis causes a watery red eye with preauricular nodes, not leukocoria.
explanation_incorrect.D: Presbyopia is an age-related accommodation disorder of adults, not a cause of leukocoria in a toddler.
explanation_incorrect.E: Open-angle glaucoma is a chronic adult optic neuropathy, not a cause of a white reflex in a child.

educationalObjective: Leukocoria in a child requires urgent evaluation for retinoblastoma (RB1, chromosome 13) and congenital cataract.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 32-year-old man with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis presents with a painful red eye, photophobia, and blurred vision. Slit-lamp examination shows inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber and a layer of pus (hypopyon).
question: Which of the following best describes his condition?

options.text: Posterior uveitis with choroiditis and retinitis
Acute angle-closure glaucoma with a mid-dilated pupil
Central retinal vein occlusion with blood-and-thunder hemorrhages
Anterior uveitis (iritis) with hypopyon, associated with an HLA-B27 condition

explanation_correct: Uveitis is inflammation of the uveal tract, named by location: anterior uveitis is iritis, while posterior uveitis is choroiditis and/or retinitis. Anterior uveitis can produce a hypopyon (pus in the anterior chamber) and conjunctival redness. It is associated with systemic inflammatory disorders such as sarcoidosis, Behçet syndrome, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and HLA-B27-associated conditions like ankylosing spondylitis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Posterior uveitis involves the choroid and retina, not the anterior chamber; this patient has anterior chamber cells and hypopyon.
explanation_incorrect.B: Allergic conjunctivitis is itchy and bilateral with discharge, not a painful eye with hypopyon.
explanation_incorrect.C: Angle-closure glaucoma causes high IOP, halos, and a mid-dilated pupil, not hypopyon with an HLA-B27 association.
explanation_incorrect.D: Retinal vein occlusion causes retinal hemorrhage and venous engorgement, not anterior chamber inflammation.

educationalObjective: Anterior uveitis (iritis) can cause hypopyon and is associated with HLA-B27 diseases, sarcoidosis, Behçet syndrome, and JIA.
